scope.method: Independent reading of current delivered artifacts, manual static command/description/pair/dedup review, standard-library inert CSV/JSON checks, selected original-source reads, and one execution of the inspected local validator with an explicit Python argument vector and no shell.
scope.safety: No collected command, shell syntax, cloud/container/database client, downloaded source code, integrator, or dataset sample was executed. No implementation or dataset files were changed. Only this report was created.

Canonical category/risk enums, class/severity values, Russian single-sentence descriptions and Bash-only command scope were inspected. SQL is not present as standalone data.

findings.details: The 1250-record target is not met: 92 accepted, deficit 1158; deny, medium, accepted explicit production-IaC, SQL-client/banking, and obfuscation coverage are absent. These limitations are explicit and permitted by the final-deliverable contract; no padding or synthetic expansion is recommended without authorization.
findings.action: Preserve the disclosed deficits and do not describe this release as target-complete or balanced.

findings.details: Azure alternatives are related safe inspection, not proven account-aligned exhaustive deletion inventories. Prefix foo does not enumerate dir/*; explicit account selection and configured defaults are not runtime-equivalence evidence. Current card/review disclosures accurately preserve this weaker relationship.
findings.action: Keep the partial-inventory and runtime-account qualifications attached to downstream use; no final-row correction is required under the documented related-inspection interpretation.

findings.details: Redis ShareAlike obligations, HF uploader-only license assertion, and dated mutable Netlify/Redis evidence are explicit residual provenance/legal limitations. Retained license/NOTICE copies and record mappings support an evidence-based inventory, not a guarantee of upstream title or legal compatibility for every downstream use.
findings.action: Distribute applicable attribution/license/provenance materials and preserve source-specific terms.

findings.details: Historical base issue text mentions absent controller context even though the command names a Deployment; the appended independent review explicitly corrects this and retains the true unresolved availability/dev-safety concern. Candidate remains excluded. This is not an accepted-data defect.
findings.action: Treat appended review and canonical integration decisions as authoritative; do not infer that rollout restart is unconditionally allow.

limitations: Audit is static and documentary. No Bash parser, live account, CLI/version binary, deployment artifact, provider implementation, webhook, plugin, storage/database service or collected command was executed.

All used source entries and retained evidence were inspected for lineage/terms consistency; this audit independently refetched selected primary examples and the provider contract, not every upstream URL, revision, license or NOTICE inventory. Most source accessibility and ownership evidence remains the explicitly qualified research/reviewer record.

Narrow credential indicators and manual excerpt inspection cannot prove complete absence of PII, secrets, incidental metadata, upstream license defects or malicious external behavior. Sensitive matches were not printed; no high-confidence credential indicator was found in raw kept material.

Global manual semantic review and narrow lexical checks cannot establish exhaustive semantic duplicate freedom or universal counterexample safety outside visible context and documented trusted-tool assumptions.

Safe counterparts may be bounded related inventories/status queries rather than complete deletion previews or equivalent successful task outcomes. Listings can be paginated, eventual, partial, context-dependent or watch indefinitely; no runtime alignment or approval is implied.

Historical proposals and risk reviews are intentionally superseded where canonical integration decisions record a correction. Pending and rejected artifacts are retained for audit and are not accepted examples.

The no-comments result is a Python tokenize fallback, not a successful unavailable omp-strip-comments run. Unit-test success is parent-reported; independent final QA did not duplicate the already passed suite.
conclusion: No blocking final-artifact inconsistency was found. The delivered 92-row subset, canonical provenance/pairs, current counts, manual decisions and dataset-card limitations are mutually consistent. Accept as a limited v0 static-documentary collection with explicit volume/coverage and provenance limitations, not as completion of the numerical target or a runtime safety guarantee.
